newsitem.title: USA: Union to appeal Valujet US flight approval.
newsitem.headline: Union to appeal Valujet US flight approval.

text.p: The Association of Flight Attendants said on Thursday it would file a court appeal to block the U.S. Transportation Department decision Thursday to allow ValuJet Inc to resume flying.
The carrier was grounded on June 17 for safety violations.
The AFA called the department's decision "a dangerous precedent that threatens airline safety."
It said it planned to ask the U.S. Court of Appeals in Washington for a stay of action to permit it time to file an appeal before the carrier was able to resume flying.

The union said the decision ignored ValuJet's past safety record and evidence that top officials president Lewis Jordan and chairman Robert Priddy hired an unqualified person, David Gentry, as vice president for maintenance.
The union had earlier protested flight approval for ValuJet.
